items.text: CNN live (21 minutes ago) confirmed: Trump said an agreement had been "largely negotiated" although specific terms are still unclear. CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed Rubio's New Delhi statement on May 23: "There's been some progress done, some progress made, even as I speak to you now, there's some work being done. There is a chance that, whether it's later today, tomorrow, in a couple days, we may have something to say, but this issue needs to be solved, as the president said, one way or another." "Largely negotiated" is Trump's most positive deal language of the 86-day war — stronger than "serious negotiations" (Day 81), stronger than "tentative progress" (Rubio, Day 84). "Largely negotiated" implies most terms are agreed. What remains: specific terms — likely Hormuz toll question, uranium disposition, sanctions timeline.

items.bold: IRAN STATE MEDIA: 35 VESSELS TRANSITED HORMUZ in past 24 hours "in coordination with Iran's naval forces." Highest single-day claim of the war.
items.text: CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed: Iranian state media claimed that 35 vessels had transited the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours in coordination with Iran's naval forces. 35 vessels in 24 hours would be the highest single-day Hormuz transit claim since February 28. For context: Kpler confirmed 55 vessels over the week of May 11-17 (~8/day). Iran now claims 35 in a single day — a 4x weekly rate increase. If verified by AIS/Kpler: Hormuz is experiencing the largest genuine reopening since the war began. The "in coordination with Iran's naval forces" language confirms the IRGC PGSA toll system is the mechanism — Iran is not opening Hormuz freely, it is managing passage through the PGSA. For India: 35 vessels/day approaches the point where Indian LPG and fertiliser carriers can transit if PGSA applications are approved.

items.bold: RUBIO CRITERIA CONFIRMED: No nuclear weapon + Hormuz WITHOUT TOLLS + TURN OVER enriched uranium. Iran-Oman mechanism confirmed.
items.text: CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed Rubio's full criteria statement: "Rubio repeated President Trump's criteria for a deal, including stopping Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, reopening the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and turning over enriched uranium." Three criteria: (1) No nuclear weapon — Iran has agreed in principle. (2) Hormuz WITHOUT TOLLS — this directly contradicts the IRGC PGSA toll system. Iran's 35-vessel transit claim is "in coordination with Iran's naval forces" = tolls are still implicit. Rubio's "without tolls" is a sticking point. (3) Turn over enriched uranium — Iran's position was to keep it within the country. The gap: Iran retaining uranium vs Rubio demanding it be "turned over." If "largely negotiated" includes a uranium disposition framework — perhaps transfer to a third country or IAEA custody rather than destruction — this may be the remaining specific term being negotiated. Iran-Oman mechanism confirmed: Tehran working with Oman "to develop a mechanism" for Hormuz transit.

items.bold: PGSA GRAPHIC (May 20): Iran published first visual map of "controlled maritime zone" spanning Hormuz. Iran-Oman mechanism in development.
items.text: CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed: a graphic shared by Iran's newly created Persian Gulf Strait Authority on May 20, 2026 shows what the authority said would be a "controlled maritime zone" spanning the Strait of Hormuz. This is the first time Iran has published a visual map of its Hormuz control architecture. The graphic formalises the IRGC's "vast operational area" doctrine (from Jask to Siri Island) into a publicly released official document. The PGSA map is Iran's legal and administrative framework for Hormuz control — it is the institutional architecture that will persist after the war ends, regardless of whether a deal is signed. Rubio's criteria of "without tolls" directly challenges this PGSA architecture. The deal negotiation is essentially: can the PGSA "controlled maritime zone" be dissolved or modified as part of the peace terms? Iran's leverage: it published the graphic after deal talks began, signalling it intends to preserve the architecture even post-deal.

military.t: TRUMP: Deal "LARGELY NEGOTIATED." RUBIO: "Whether Today, Tomorrow, in a Couple Days." Most Positive War-End Signal of 86 Days.
military.d: CNN live (21 minutes ago) and CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed: Trump said an agreement had been "largely negotiated" although specific terms are still unclear. Rubio, speaking in New Delhi on May 23 (confirmed with photo), stated: "There's been some progress done, some progress made, even as I speak to you now, there's some work being done. There is a chance that, whether it's later today, tomorrow, in a couple days, we may have something to say, but this issue needs to be solved, as the president said, one way or another." "Largely negotiated" is Trump's strongest deal language of the 86-day war. Rubio "days away" is the tightest timeline commitment any official has made. Combined: a deal announcement within 24-96 hours is now the base case. What remains "specific terms": likely Hormuz toll vs no-toll framework and uranium disposition mechanism.

military.t: IRAN: 35 Vessels Transited Hormuz in Past 24 Hours "In Coordination with Naval Forces." Highest Single-Day Claim.
military.d: CBS News live (30 minutes ago) confirmed: Iranian state media claimed 35 vessels had transited the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours in coordination with Iran's naval forces. 35/day vs Kpler's 8/day average for May 11-17 = 4x improvement if verified. Still 22% of pre-war 130-160/day but the largest single-day transit claim of the war. "In coordination with Iran's naval forces" = PGSA toll system managing the transit. Iran is demonstrating it can selectively open Hormuz as a deal incentive. The 35-vessel claim serves two purposes: (1) Shows the world Iran can operate a managed Hormuz opening, (2) Provides Trump political cover to announce a deal ("Hormuz is opening as part of our negotiations"). Rubio criteria "without tolls" remains the gap — Iran's 35 vessels are almost certainly toll-paying PGSA-coordinated transits.

military.t: RUBIO CRITERIA + PGSA "Controlled Maritime Zone" Graphic = The Remaining Negotiation Gap.
military.d: CBS News live confirmed both: (1) Rubio criteria: no nuclear weapon, Hormuz WITHOUT TOLLS, turn over enriched uranium. (2) PGSA published "controlled maritime zone" graphic on May 20 showing Hormuz as an Iran-managed waterway. The negotiation gap in plain terms: Rubio wants Hormuz WITHOUT tolls. Iran's PGSA graphic claims Hormuz as a "controlled maritime zone." These are irreconcilable unless a deal explicitly disbands the PGSA. Uranium: Rubio says "turn over" — Iran said "keep within the country." "Largely negotiated" implies most other terms agreed (ceasefire, sanctions timeline, military withdrawal). The two remaining sticking points: PGSA tolls + uranium disposition. If Iran agrees to: (1) suspend PGSA tolls for 5-10 years under IAEA monitoring, (2) transfer enriched uranium to a third country or IAEA custody — a deal can be announced this week.

assessment.headline: DAY 86, 10:40PM SUN: TRUMP: "LARGELY NEGOTIATED." RUBIO: "WHETHER TODAY, TOMORROW, DAYS AWAY." IRAN: 35 VESSELS TRANSITED HORMUZ IN 24 HOURS. BRENT $100 — CNN: TRADERS MAY TEST $94 FLOOR MONDAY. INDIA MONDAY: LARGEST GAP-UP OF 86-DAY WAR EXPECTED.
assessment.body:
Sunday 10:40 PM IST. Day 86. The war may be ending.

THE TRUMP SIGNAL
"Largely negotiated" — most positive deal language of 86 days.
Stronger than "serious negotiations" (Day 81).
Stronger than "tentative progress" (Rubio, Day 84).
"Largely" implies most terms are agreed.
What remains: specific terms — PGSA tolls vs Rubio "without tolls," uranium disposition.

THE RUBIO STATEMENT — IN NEW DELHI
Rubio in New Delhi (photo confirmed, May 23):
"There is a chance that, whether it's later today, tomorrow, in a couple days, we may have something to say."
This is a 24-96 hour deal window.
Rubio also confirmed US criteria: no nuclear weapon + Hormuz WITHOUT TOLLS + TURN OVER uranium.
"One way or the other" — deal or force.

THE IRAN 35-VESSEL SIGNAL
Iranian state media: 35 vessels in 24 hours "in coordination with naval forces."
If verified: 4x the May 11-17 Kpler weekly average.
22% of pre-war 130-160/day but the highest single-day claim of the war.
Iran demonstrating it can open Hormuz selectively as a deal incentive.
The catch: "in coordination with naval forces" = PGSA tolls still apply.
Rubio wants "without tolls." Gap on the mechanism remains.

THE PGSA GRAPHIC
Iran published the first visual map of its "controlled maritime zone" May 20.
This is Iran's institutional claim to Hormuz sovereignty — made public even while a deal is being negotiated.
Iran is negotiating a deal while simultaneously publishing the legal architecture for continued control. This tells you Iran's post-deal intent: PGSA persists even after hostilities end.

WHAT A DEAL MEANS FOR INDIA
Brent: $100 → $88-92 on deal. OMC losses eliminated on petrol at Brent $88. Diesel under-recovery reduced from Rs 35/L to Rs 8-10/L.
Rupee: 95.50 → 93.00 on deal. Import bill reduction: ~$50 billion annually at Brent $88 vs $100.
Sensex: +1,500-2,000 pts (76,900-77,400) on deal confirmation.
Kharif fertiliser: Gulf sourcing fully viable at $88 Brent. PGSA applications may become unnecessary if tolls suspended.

THE REMAINING GAP
Rubio: Hormuz WITHOUT TOLLS + TURN OVER uranium.
Iran: PGSA "controlled maritime zone" + uranium stays within country.
"Largely negotiated" means these two gaps are being bridged — or Trump is calling something "largely negotiated" that Iran will dispute.

VERDICT: Day 86 Sunday night is the most consequential overnight of the 86-day war for India. Trump has said "largely negotiated." Rubio has said "days away." Iran has shown 35 vessels transiting. Brent is at $100 and CNN says traders will probe $94 on Monday. If the deal is confirmed before India's 9:15 AM open: the Sensex will record its largest single-day gain since April 8. India's 86-day energy emergency may be entering its final chapter. But the PGSA graphic — published by Iran on May 20 — is Iran's reminder that even after the war ends, the Hormuz of 2026 will not be the Hormuz of 2025. The chokepoint has changed. The deal will close the war. It will not undo the architecture.
